shadows.name: paper-under

shadows.name: paper-tab

shadows.name: header-strip

shadows.name: contact-sheet
shadows.purpose: Ruby contact sheet casting upward over the page, following the scalloped edge (CSS filter).

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The only curve. Critically damped, no overshoot: folds, underline growth, arrow nudge.

motion.name: unfold
motion.purpose: Fold flap opening. Hero on load with 0.35s delay; others scroll-scrubbed (view timeline, entry 15% to cover 48%) or opened by IntersectionObserver at 35% visibility.

motion.name: underline-grow
motion.purpose: Nav link hover bar drawn in from the left.

motion.name: link-thicken
motion.purpose: Email link underline thickening and arrow nudge on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All fold transforms, filters and link transitions removed; paper is simply flat.

components.name: The Fold
components.description: Signature: a mirror-symmetric papercut whose right half unfolds over the fixed left half along the axis, settling flat with no overshoot.
components.css: .ds-fold { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 220px; perspective: 2800px; background: #fbfbf9; } .ds-fold-half { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; } .ds-fold-fixed { clip-path: inset(-25% -0.5px -25% -25%); } .ds-fold-flap { transform-origin: 0 50%; clip-path: inset(-25% -25% -25% -0.5px); animation: ds-unfold 1.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) 0.35s both; } .ds-fold:hover .ds-fold-flap { animation: none; } .ds-top { fill: #e30613; filter: drop-shadow(0 7px 7px rgb(90 0 16 / 0.32)); } .ds-under { fill: #9e0a16; filter: drop-shadow(0 3px 3px rgb(90 0 16 / 0.25)); } @keyframes ds-unfold { from { transform: rotateY(-180deg); filter: brightness(0.82); } 50% { filter: brightness(0.7); } to { transform: rotateY(0deg); filter: brightness(1); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-fold-flap { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Rubinowe is one sheet of ruby paper, folded once along a vertical axis and cut with precision. Every ornament is a mirror-symmetric papercut (rosette, tree, ladder, birds, lattice) whose cuts are drawn from code glyphs: braces, angle brackets, square brackets. The cut is exact and geometric, never folk-soft. The page around the art is plain white paper with heavy, tight grotesque headlines and a calm workhorse body; the papercut carries the voice, the type carries the facts.

Depth is physical, not tonal. Paper lies on paper and casts a real shadow, cuts are real holes the shadow falls through, and state is shown by form (folded, cut, flat) rather than by a new hue. The signature behaviour is the fold: each papercut opens from its folded right half along the mirror axis, on load for the hero and driven by scroll for every other section, settling flat with critical damping and no overshoot. The last section is the same sheet reversed: drenched ruby with a scalloped top edge and a white-paper rosette cut into it.

Density is low and the rhythm generous. Sections breathe on a fluid section unit, copy columns stay narrow (34 to 44ch), and composition is asymmetric except where the fold demands mirroring.
keyCharacteristics: Four flat inks only: paper, ruby, deep ruby, ink (plus a soft ink for secondary text).
Papercut art built from code glyphs, mirror-symmetric about x = 0, folded at the axis.
Real cast shadows between paper layers; no tonal shading, no gradients in the art.
Display set heavy and narrow (Bricolage Grotesque 800, wdth 88, negative tracking).
Dotted perforation lines are the only rules.
One motion curve, critically damped: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).

rules.name: The Two Papers Rule
rules.body: Art uses exactly two paper colours per surface: a top layer and an under layer (ruby over deep ruby on white; white paper over deep ruby on the contact sheet). No midtones, no tints, no gradients inside a papercut.

rules.name: The Reversal Rule
rules.body: On a ruby ground the sheet reverses: the top paper becomes white and the under layer stays deep ruby. Achieve it by setting `--cut-top` and `--cut-under` on the art container, never by redrawing the motif.

rules.name: The Hard-Stop Rule
rules.body: CSS gradient functions appear only as hard-edged devices: punched holes, perforation dots, the solid underline bar. A gradient that blends one colour into another is outside the world.

rules.name: The Cut Letter Rule
rules.body: Every display-face setting uses weight 700 to 800, `font-variation-settings: "wdth" 88`, and negative tracking (-0.025em to -0.04em). Headlines use `text-wrap: balance`, paragraphs `text-wrap: pretty`.

rules.name: The Address Is The Button Rule
rules.body: The primary action is the email address itself, set in the display face with a thick underline. There are no filled buttons.

rules.name: The Real Paper Rule
rules.body: A shadow exists only where one paper lies over another. It is soft, warm (rgb 90 0 16), and offset in the direction of the overlap; never a hard offset block, never a glow.

rules.name: The Folding Shade Rule
rules.body: While a flap is mid-fold it darkens (brightness 0.82 to 0.7) and returns to 1 when flat. This is transient light on moving paper, not a static midtone.

dos: Do build every ornament as a mirror-symmetric papercut about x = 0, cut from code glyphs ({ } < > [ ]), with cuts as SVG mask holes.
Do keep art to two paper layers per surface: top (ruby, or white paper on ruby) and under (deep ruby), switched only via `--cut-top` / `--cut-under`.
Do cast shadows only where paper overlaps paper, in warm rgb(90 0 16) at 0.18 to 0.35 alpha.
Do set the display face at 700 to 800, wdth 88, negative tracking.
Do make the email address the primary action, set in the display face and underlined.
Do separate list rows with dotted perforation lines (1.5px dots, 11px repeat).
Do animate with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) only, and leave every fold flat under reduced motion.
donts: Don't add midtones, tints, or colour-blending gradients to the art or surfaces; gradient functions are allowed only as hard-stop holes, dots, and bars.
Don't use solid or hairline borders as dividers; perforation is the only rule.
Don't use overshoot or spring easing on folds; paper settles flat.
Don't use hard offset block shadows, glows, or neutral grey shadows.
Don't use filled or pill buttons; actions are underlined text.
Don't introduce colours beyond paper, ruby, deep ruby, ink, and soft ink.
Don't let a fold half bleed past its axis; each half is clipped at the fold.
